Polynomial domains and rings

Source: vignettes/polynomial-domains.Rmd
polynomial-domains.Rmd
library(symcompR)
x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y")

This vignette covers sympy.polys.domains, sympy.polys.rings, sympy.polys.fields, and sympy.polys.orderings: the coefficient domains behind Poly, and the sparse polynomial rings that the algorithms use.

Domains

Coefficient domains are objects: ZZ, QQ, GF(p), polynomial rings ZZ[x], fraction fields, and algebraic fields.

ZZ[x]
#> ZZ[x]
GF(7)(3) * GF(7)(5)
#> 1 mod 7
frac_field(QQ, x)
#> QQ(x)
algebraic_field(QQ, sqrt(S(2)))
#> QQ<sqrt(2)>
construct_domain(list(1, Rational(1, 2)))[[1]]
#> QQ

ring() creates a sparse polynomial ring and its generators, the low level representation that the algorithms use.

R <- ring("x,y", ZZ)
R[[1]]
#> Polynomial ring in x, y over ZZ with lex order
X <- R[[2]]; Y <- R[[3]]
(X + Y)^2
#> x^2 + 2*x*y + y^2

Domain constructors

Each SymPy domain class has a constructor. The integer and rational domains exist in “python” and “gmpy” flavors in SymPy; here they all give the same domain.

IntegerRing()
#> ZZ
RationalField()
#> QQ
RealField()
#> RR
ComplexField()
#> CC
RR
#> RR
CC
#> CC
ZZ_I
#> ZZ_I
QQ_I
#> QQ_I
EX
#> EX
EXRAW
#> EXRAW
ExpressionDomain()
#> EX
FiniteField(5)
#> GF(5)
FF(5)
#> GF(5)
FractionField(ZZ, x)
#> ZZ(x)
PolynomialRing(QQ, x, y)
#> QQ[x,y]
poly_ring(ZZ, x)
#> ZZ[x]
AlgebraicField(QQ, sqrt(S(3)))
#> QQ<sqrt(3)>
CyclotomicField(5)
#> QQ<zeta5>
Domain(ZZ)
#> [1] TRUE
Domain(3)
#> [1] FALSE
list(ZZ_python(), ZZ_gmpy(), GMPYIntegerRing(), PythonIntegerRing(),
     QQ_python(), QQ_gmpy(), GMPYRationalField())
#> [[1]]
#> ZZ
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> ZZ
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> ZZ
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> ZZ
#> 
#> [[5]]
#> QQ
#> 
#> [[6]]
#> QQ
#> 
#> [[7]]
#> QQ
list(FF_python(3), FF_gmpy(3), GMPYFiniteField(3), PythonFiniteField(3))
#> [[1]]
#> GF(3)
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> GF(3)
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> GF(3)
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> GF(3)
PythonRational(3, 6)
#> Big Rational ('bigq') :
#> [1] 1/2

from_sympy() converts an expression into a domain element and to_sympy() converts it back.

a <- from_sympy(QQ, Rational(3, 4))
a
#> Big Rational ('bigq') :
#> [1] 3/4
to_sympy(QQ, a)
#> 3/4
to_sympy(GF(7), GF(7)(10))
#> 3

Polynomial rings and fields

ring() and xring() create a ring and its generators, vring() also assigns the generators to variables, and sring() builds the ring from expressions. field(), xfield(), vfield(), and sfield() are the counterparts for rational function fields.

R <- xring("x,y", ZZ)
R[[1]]
#> Polynomial ring in x, y over ZZ with lex order
X <- R[[2]][[1]]; Y <- R[[2]][[2]]
(X + Y)^2
#> x^2 + 2*x*y + y^2
vring("u,v", QQ)
#> Polynomial ring in u, v over QQ with lex order
(u - v)^3
#> u^3 - 3*u^2*v + 3*u*v^2 - v^3
sring(list(x^2 + 2 * y, x / 3))
#> [[1]]
#> Polynomial ring in x, y over QQ with lex order
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> x^2 + 2*y
#> 
#> [[2]][[2]]
#> 1/3*x
K <- xfield("s,t", ZZ)
K[[2]][[1]] / K[[2]][[2]]
#> s/t
vfield("p", QQ)
#> Rational function field in p over QQ with lex order
1 / (p + 1)
#> 1/(p + 1)
sfield(list(x / y, 1 / x))
#> [[1]]
#> Rational function field in x, y over ZZ with lex order
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> x/y
#> 
#> [[2]][[2]]
#> 1/x
Kf <- field("u,v", QQ)
Kf[[1]]
#> Rational function field in u, v over QQ with lex order
Kf[[2]] / Kf[[3]] + 1
#> (u + v)/v

Monomials and orderings

Monomial() is an exponent vector with optional generators. The ordering keys ilex(), igrlex(), and igrevlex() sort monomials in the inverse of the lexicographic, graded lexicographic, and graded reverse lexicographic orders.

m <- Monomial(c(1, 2))
m
#> Monomial((1, 2))
Monomial(c(2, 0, 1), list(x, y, Symbol("z")))
#> Monomial((2, 0, 1))
ilex(c(1, 2))
#> [1] -1 -2
igrlex(c(1, 2))
#> [1] -3 -1 -2
igrevlex(c(1, 2))
#> [1] -3  2  1

Options() is the option manager that Poly uses to process generators and flags.

Options(list(x, y), list(domain = "QQ"))
#> $gens
#> $gens[[1]]
#> x
#> 
#> $gens[[2]]
#> y
#> 
#> 
#> $expand
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $greedy
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $auto
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $strict
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $frac
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $formal
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $polys
#> NULL
#> 
#> $include
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $all
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $order
#> [1] "lex"
#> 
#> $domain
#> QQ
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "sym_poly_options"
